candidates.attacker_control: The parsed document is whatever XML is handed to the processor: a file/classpath resource name supplied to processFile*/processStreamAndScheduleJobs (e.g. an upload/widget/administration endpoint that forwards user XML to this public API), or the quartz job-data XML file configured for XMLSchedulingDataProcessorPlugin (default quartz_data.xml, optionally rescanned on scanInterval). Any party able to influence that XML file/resource/stream controls the DOCTYPE and entity declarations.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Repository-wide literal searches found no DOCTYPE handling, no setFeature call, no XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA, no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, no EntityResolver, and no setXIncludeAware/setExpandEntityReferences anywhere. XMLSchedulingDataProcessor is the only DocumentBuilderFactory/XML parser in the tree, so there is no alternate hardened parser being used for this data. The schema setup (lines 173-175) uses a locally packaged XSD when available (resolveSchemaSource, lines 216-237) with an online fallback URL, but schema validation does not disable DOCTYPE/external entity resolution; setValidating(true) can additionally cause external DTD retrieval. No input pre-scanning, filtering or sanitization of the stream exists before parse. No test/build execution was performed, so the behavior was not runtime-confirmed.
candidates.impact: XML External Entity processing while parsing job-scheduling data: disclosure of local files whose content is expanded into parsed values (job/trigger metadata, job data) or surfaced through parse/validation errors and debug logs; server-side request forgery against internal HTTP/file endpoints via external entities or external DTD; and denial of service through entity expansion (e.g. nested entity bombs). The parser is a library component, so impact is inherited by every application that feeds it XML from a less-trusted source.
candidates.prerequisites: An application must expose XMLSchedulingDataProcessor to XML that an attacker can influence (plugin file in a writable/shared location, or embedded use of the public processFile/processStream APIs with untrusted XML), and must run on a JAXP implementation whose defaults allow DOCTYPE processing/external entity resolution (the standard behavior; no hardening is applied in code). No authentication or special privilege is needed beyond the ability to supply the XML document.
candidates.root_cause: XMLSchedulingDataProcessor.initDocumentParser() (lines 166-177) builds the DocumentBuilderFactory from the JAXP defaults and only calls setNamespaceAware(true), setValidating(true), and the two schemaLanguage/schemaSource attributes. It never calls disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities=false, external-parameter-entities=false, load-external-dtd=false, setXIncludeAware/setExpandEntityReferences(false), or XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA, and it sets no EntityResolver. The resulting DocumentBuilder is then used at line 494 (docBuilder.parse(is)) for any XML supplied to the public entry points, so any DOCTYPE/internal-subset entity or external DTD in that XML is honored and resolved.
candidates.title: XXE: XMLSchedulingDataProcessor parses job-scheduling XML with an unhardened DocumentBuilder (external entities/DTD enabled)
candidates.trace: 1) XMLSchedulingDataProcessorPlugin.processFile (line 306) -> processor.processFileAndScheduleJobs(fileName, fileName, scheduler) (line 319); JobFile.initialize (lines 370-408) resolves the name as a filesystem File or classloader URL. 2) XMLSchedulingDataProcessor.processFileAndScheduleJobs(String,String,Scheduler) (line 840) -> processFile(fileName, systemId) (lines 445-460) -> new InputSource(getInputStream(fileName)) with a caller/systemId -> process(is). 3) process(InputSource) (lines 491-494) executes docBuilder.parse(is). 4) docBuilder came from initDocumentParser (lines 166-177) with entities/DTD unrestricted. 5) Entity values are expanded into the DOM and then read by the XPath extraction code (e.g. job/trigger name, description, job-data value parsing around lines 590-700) and can appear in debug logging (e.g. line 628-629) and in ValidationException/error handling; entity references can also trigger outbound fetches (SSRF) and expansion blowups (DoS).
candidates.unverified: Whether a given deployment actually lets an attacker influence the processed XML (plugin file writability/scanInterval re-read, or an application embedding the public API) was not verifiable from source alone; exploitability is therefore deployment-dependent. Actual file-read exfiltration path (which parsed value/error is returned to the attacker) and JAXP implementation defaults were not confirmed at runtime; no exploit was executed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the full 457-file snapshot (source root parity confirmed; no over-5-MiB, symlink, or name/path exclusions, and 300 Java files parsed by the P1 index with complete index status). Modules covered: quartz-core (xml, impl/jdbcjobstore, core, impl/triggers/calendar/matchers, simpl, utils, ee/servlet+ee/jta, spi), quartz-plugins (xml initializer, history, interrupt, management), quartz-jobs (mail, jms, ejb, jmx, native, file/directory scan), quartz-oracle/weblogic/jboss/commonj, terracotta bootstrap (clustered job store and collections), management-quartz/-impl, distribution examples, plus docs, POMs, properties and SQL scripts. Targeted searches were run for XML parser construction and hardening (DocumentBuilderFactory/XMLReader/SAXParser, setFeature, ACCESS_EXTERNAL, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, EntityResolver, DOCTYPE), deserialization (ObjectInputStream, SerializationHelper), command execution (Runtime/ProcessBuilder), SQL sinks (createStatement/executeQuery/string-built SQL), reflection (Class.forName/newInstance), and request-parameter/HTTP handling. Test sources are not present in the snapshot, so test evidence could not be examined. The P1 relation index is syntax-only (no control/data flow, no semantic resolution, 9,014 unresolved calls), so reachability and data flow were verified by reading source text rather than relying on index edges.
limitations: Static review only: no compilation, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run, so the XXE behavior and its impact are not runtime-confirmed.

Attacker influence over the processed XML depends on the consuming application/deployment (plugin file location and permissions, or embedded use of the public API); this cannot be established from the snapshot alone.

The P1 index provides syntax/navigation candidates only (no control-flow or data-flow, semantic resolution not implemented, 9,014 unresolved calls), so some call paths into the parser and other sinks may be unreported or unverified.
No test sources are included in the snapshot; TestCategories.properties references tests (e.g. XMLSchedulingDataProcessorTest) that are not present, so test-based corroboration was impossible.
Dependency-level issues (e.g. c3p0/HikariCP/slf4j/javax.mail versions in the POMs) and non-Java assets were only spot-checked and were not assessed for known CVEs.
No external patch, advisory, CVE, or sibling-run information was consulted; the CVE association noted for context is not part of the source evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe Java deserialization of job data from the JDBC job store: StdJDBCDelegate.getObjectFromBlob/deserializeJobData (ObjectInputStream.readObject around lines 3195-3203), plus HSQLDBDelegate, MSSQLDelegate, SybaseDelegate, PostgreSQLDelegate, CUBRIDDelegate, CacheDelegate, PointbaseDelegate, OracleDelegate and WebLogicDelegate equivalents.
rejected_leads.reason: The serialized bytes come from the scheduler's own job-store tables, which Quartz treats as a trusted persistence store (writing them requires the same DB/SQL access that already permits broad manipulation). No source evidence shows untrusted external input reaching these readers, so this is a design/trust-boundary risk rather than a clear vulnerability in this snapshot.

Keys are JobKey/TriggerKey values written by Quartz itself and read back from the Terracotta cluster store; reaching the marker-prefixed string path with attacker-controlled data requires write access to the trusted clustered store. No data flow from an untrusted caller was verified.

rejected_leads.lead: Job data driven command execution / reflection: NativeJob Runtime.exec (lines 171-174), EJBInvokerJob, JMXInvokerJob, and PropertySettingJobFactory/Util property setting from JobDataMap keys.
rejected_leads.reason: These are documented features that execute the job data the scheduler is explicitly asked to run; an attacker who controls JobDataMap content already controls job definitions, so no additional privilege boundary is crossed in the library itself.

rejected_leads.lead: QuartzSchedulerMBeanImpl uses Class.forName(...).newInstance() on class names taken from JMX attribute maps (lines 210-320).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only through JMX MBean operations, which are expected to be authenticated/privileged; no missing-check evidence beyond the privileged interface contract.

rejected_leads.lead: resolveSchemaSource fallback to a remote schema URL (http://www.quartz-scheduler.org/xml/job_scheduling_data_2_0.xsd, lines 216-237).
rejected_leads.reason: The URL is a hard-coded constant, not attacker-controlled; only a robustness/network-dependency concern, not an injection sink.

summary: The snapshot is Quartz Scheduler 2.4.0-SNAPSHOT (457 files, 300 Java files). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an unhardened JAXP XML parser in org.quartz.xml.XMLSchedulingDataProcessor: the DocumentBuilderFactory is created and configured only with namespaceAware/validating/schema attributes, and the document is parsed with no DOCTYPE restriction, no external-entity disablement, no ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* restriction, and no EntityResolver (verified by repository-wide searches that return zero hits for setFeature, ACCESS_EXTERNAL, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, EntityResolver, expand-entity/XInclude hardening, or any DOCTYPE check). The class is the library's job-scheduling XML loader and is reachable both from the public API (processFileAndScheduleJobs / processStreamAndScheduleJobs) and from XMLSchedulingDataProcessorPlugin, which loads job XML from the filesystem/classpath and can re-parse it periodically. A DOCTYPE/external entity in the processed XML is therefore resolved, giving XXE (local file disclosure via entity expansion into parsed job values/logs, SSRF, and entity-expansion DoS). This matches the well-known failure fixed in later Quartz releases (CVE-2019-13990 class); no runtime confirmation was performed. Other severe-looking areas (JobDataMap blob deserialization in the JDBC/Terracotta stores, NativeJob/reflection-based jobs) require control of stores/data that Quartz treats as trusted and were left as rejected leads.
